Aixtron appears to be one of the cleanest pure tool-layer exposures but is not a clean US-exchange-listed candidate; keep it as a non-US/OTC context anchor and use it to identify US-listed customers or adjacent equipment suppliers.

TSEM is a US-listed silicon-photonics foundry candidate with official 1.6T AI/datacenter announcements; later layers should test whether SiPho revenue is large enough to matter within the broader specialty-foundry model.
SMTC is a mixed-label signal-integrity supplier with 1.6T optical-interconnect TIA exposure; later layers should verify socket share and segment contribution.

The optical-interconnect chokepoint map should separate module assembly, laser/component supply, silicon-photonics foundry capacity, signal-integrity chips, compound-semiconductor substrates, and MOCVD/epitaxy tools; scarcity may not sit where headline attention is highest.

Aixtron-like epitaxy-tool exposure is central to the node but not cleanly US-listed; VECO is the most relevant US-listed equipment hypothesis found in this pass, while Aixtron remains a non-US/ADR context name for competitive benchmarking.

Reference lane includes direct optical component and laser leaders that the market likely already associates with AI networking. Underfollowed lane emphasizes manufacturing, RF/analog signal-chain, and component suppliers one step away from hyperscaler AI headlines. AIXTRON appears important to the epitaxy-tool bottleneck in the external context, but it is not included as a main candidate because the task asks for US-listed companies; it should remain a non-US/OTC coverage-gap comparator in later work.
